anatomy.intro: A Lithops head packs its water reserve and light-gathering surfaces into just two fleshy leaves.

parts.function: Two thickened leaves form one water-storing head.
parts.label: Paired fleshy leaves

parts.function: Translucent areas admit light to tissue inside the leaves.
parts.label: Upper windows

parts.function: Replacement growth and flowers emerge between the leaves.
parts.label: Central fissure

parts.function: A taproot and finer roots anchor the head and absorb water.
parts.label: Root system

flowers.text: Typical L. lesliei flowers are yellow and emerge from the central fissure. Lithops blooms open on sunny afternoons, briefly turning an inconspicuous stone-like body into a conspicuous flower.

growth.note: Watch the tan and grey groups individually as their repeating leaf cycles unfold; new leaves matter more than the month.

stages.text: A head maintains its paired leaves rather than a stem full of foliage.
stages.title: Leaf body

stages.text: Replacement leaves form within the old pair and draw on its reserves.
stages.title: Internal renewal

stages.text: The old leaves dry into a sheath; renewal may also produce extra heads.
stages.title: New body exposed

habitat.text: Lithops lesliei grows from southeastern Botswana into South Africa’s Free State, in dry shrubland and desert environments. Its low body and patterned upper surfaces suit a life close to the stony ground.

image.alt: One tan-patterned Lithops head with numbered paired leaves, upper windows, central fissure and roots.

A subtle cutaway ground line shows the generic single tapering taproot with fine lateral roots, without a pot. Four crisp numbered callouts with thin clean leader lines, one each: 1 points to the fleshy leaf body; 2 points specifically to the patterned upper window surface; 3 points to the central fissure; 4 points to the schematic taproot and side-root system below soil. Numerals 1,2,3,4 only, each once in a small high-contrast ochre/forest-green round badge. Reserve generous whitespace around the central drawing, avoid any overlap of leader lines, make number positions obvious. lookalikes.name: Lithops aucampiae
lookalikes.text: Also brown and channel-patterned, L. aucampiae overlaps in appearance with L. lesliei; surface markings alone can be difficult to separate.

lookalikes.name: Probable Lithops salicola
lookalikes.text: The neighboring grey group has broader, more open windows than the tan patterned heads.

mature.text: A head stays low and compact, and successive leaf renewals can gradually produce a small cluster. Growth becomes especially easy to follow when the new fissure appears roughly at right angles to the old one.

milestones.text: Purchased at Home Depot in Howell, Michigan, from Altman Plants nursery stock.
milestones.title: Home Depot arrival

milestones.text: Moved into the Blush Mauve planter with the other appearance group; all four heads were described as firm.
milestones.title: Shared repot

nameStory.text: The species first carried the name Mesembryanthemum lesliei in 1912; its accepted combination in Lithops followed in 1922.
